mechanism.summary: Append one stack-based discarded-binary-branch superinstruction and derive it only for the exact Binary; JumpIfFalse; Pop shape whose false target is also a Pop. The existing lowered execution stream keeps every source instruction offset while the fused operation evaluates the same binary expression, applies the same truthiness test, discards the condition, and advances directly past the Pop on either edge. Existing local-local comparison fusion runs first, so this unit covers the remaining property, global, constant, and mixed-source conditions without replacing its stronger four-operation fusion.
mechanism.generality: Selection depends only on immutable bytecode control flow, the existing complete flow analysis, and the exact two-edge discard shape. It applies to every eligible function and never inspects source paths, benchmark or function names, property names, operand values, iteration counts, checksums, or expected results. The immutable source bytecode and all specialized loop plans remain unchanged; incomplete analysis, non-linear instruction ranges, unmatched Pop edges, malformed targets, suspension-sensitive code, and every nonmatching branch retain the original Binary and JumpIfFalse operations.
semantic_risks: preserving left-to-right binary coercion, exceptions, Proxy and valueOf effects, and exact BinaryOp semantics before testing truthiness
discarding the computed value exactly once on both branch edges while preserving the operand stack seen at every merge target
preserving catchable stack-underflow and malformed-instruction errors rather than turning them into unchecked indexing
keeping original bytecode offsets, jump targets, source spans, and specialized loop-plan recognition unchanged
letting the existing local-local comparison superinstruction win before this more general stack-based fusion
appending one Op variant without changing size_of::<Op>() or causing a dispatch-layout regression larger than the removed operations

profile_evidence.shared_cost: HashMap executes 5,122,209 Binary followed by JumpIfFalse sequences whose fallthrough and false-target instructions are both Pop. Replacing each three-dispatch path with one derived operation removes a theoretical 10,244,418 of 105,261,606 generic dispatches, or 9.73 percent, while preserving both branch destinations and the original binary evaluator.
